t.6.8.1: Then the rākṣasa named Prahasta, who resembled a dark rain-cloud, the valiant commander of the army, spoke these words with joined palms.
t.6.8.2: Neither gods, Dānavas nor Gandharvas, neither Piśācas, birds nor serpents are able to overcome you; how much less, then, the monkeys in battle!
t.6.8.3: We were all careless and trusting, and so we were deceived by Hanumān. As long as I live, that forest-roamer would not have gone away alive.
t.6.8.4: I shall make the whole earth, bounded by the ocean, with its mountains, woods and forests, empty of monkeys; let Your Honour only command me.
t.6.8.5: And I shall surely provide protection from the monkey, O night-roamer; no sorrow at all born of your own offense will come to you.
t.6.8.6: And a rākṣasa named Durmukha, greatly enraged, said: "This assault upon all of us is indeed not to be forgiven."
t.6.8.8: This very moment I alone shall slay the monkeys and return, even if they have entered the terrible ocean, the sky, or Rasātala.
t.6.8.7: This assault by the lord of the monkeys is once more a humiliation for the city and the inner palace of the lord of the rākṣasas, glorious ones that we are.
t.6.8.9: Then the mighty Vajradaṃṣṭra, greatly enraged, seized a terrible iron club smeared with flesh and blood and spoke.
t.6.8.11: Today, alone, having thrown the army of monkeys into turmoil and slain Rāma together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa with my iron club, I shall return.
t.6.8.10: What concern of yours is Hanumān, that pitiable wretch, while the invincible Rāma still stands, and Sugrīva together with Lakṣmaṇa?
t.6.8.12: Then the heroic and mighty son of Kumbhakarṇa, Nikumbha by name, supremely enraged, spoke to Rāvaṇa, who made the worlds cry out.
t.6.8.13: Let all of you remain here together with the great king; I alone shall slay Rāghava along with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.8.14: Then a rākṣasa named Vajrahanu, huge as a mountain, enraged and licking his mouth all round with his tongue, spoke these words.
t.6.8.15: Let your honors attend to your affairs at ease, free from anxiety; I alone shall devour all those leaders of the monkey hordes.
t.6.8.16: Let them be at ease and free from care, let them sport and drink the honeyed vāruṇī wine; I alone will slay Sugrīva together with Lakṣmaṇa, along with Aṅgada and Hanūmān, and Rāma too, that elephant in battle.
